kernel: five-point Jacobi: (center+north+south+west+east)*0.2, float64; zero Dirichlet boundary
traffic_assumptions: 24 B assumes each source loaded once, one 8 B destination RFO plus 8 B writeback; 48 B assumes five independent 8 B source loads plus one 8 B store. These are alternative models, not measured DRAM traffic. NumPy uses multiple passes and can add traffic.
cache_residency_warning: If grids fit shared cache, DRAM Roofline is insufficient; use a cache-level Roofline. Barriers, Python/NumPy dispatch and scheduler overhead can also dominate.
classification: conditional memory-bandwidth-bound: low AI, hardware ridge point unavailable
evidence_status: analytical traffic estimate only; no hardware counter proof
weak_scaling_note: PDF expression P*Work(1)*T1/(Work(P)*TP) approaches weak efficiency T1/TP when Work(P)=P*Work(1). Conventional scaled speedup is Work(P)/Work(1)*T1/TP. Both are preserved.

scaling_fit.method: least squares on T_P/T_1 = 1/P + s*(1-1/P); s constrained to [0,1]
scaling_fit.model_warning: Amdahl fit is descriptive; heterogeneous cores, barriers and memory traffic violate ideal assumptions.
scaling_fit.timing_scope: spawn, allocation, initialization and reference excluded; start signal, 100 update steps with per-step barriers, and completion notification included

cache_footprint_analysis.interpretation: The two 1472x1472 float64 grids occupy 34,668,544 bytes, exceeding either cluster L2; no global shared L3 was reported by sysctl. This favors a memory-traffic interpretation but does not prove DRAM bandwidth saturation.
cache_footprint_analysis.peak_status: CPU FP64 peak and nominal memory bandwidth were not measured or supplied; no definitive Roofline bottleneck claim is made.

verification_storage: Large arrays are not included. The verifier reruns numerical kernels and independently rebuilds references, then compares their salted SHA-256 values with the digests recorded in the original measured results. Timings are not regenerated by verification.
